discovery: Prediction and discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting phases in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (twistronics)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics / two-dimensional van der Waals materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the moire superlattice of bilayer graphene produces nearly flat electronic bands. Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers (Nature 2018) confirmed this, finding correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched on and off with a gate voltage. The work showed that the twist angle between atomic layers is a new, continuously tunable control parameter for quantum phases. The same material can be driven between metal, insulator, superconductor and orbital magnet electrostatically, without chemical doping. The idea has since spread to moire transition-metal dichalcogenides and rhombohedral graphene, where it produced the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect and other new states. By turning crystal geometry into a design variable for strongly correlated physics, these discoveries opened the field of twistronics and changed how van der Waals devices are conceived.
